name: Enna Consulting
tagline: Trilingual showcase for an HR consultant: one fluid page, but a real URL per section and language to be found and shared in Belgium
role: For a consultant in talent acquisition, diversity and employer branding, I designed a site that explains a three-axis offer in minutes and leads naturally to contact. A Next.js one-pager in FR/NL/EN: single-page fluidity plus 9 real pages for Google (3 languages × 3 sections), each with hreflang and structured data. V1 in 3 days, then refined through the ennabv.be domain (44 commits, 3 PRs).

meta.title: Enna Consulting · Case study
meta.description: Trilingual one-pager for an HR consultant: per-section URLs, international SEO and accessibility.

paragraphs: Enna Consulting helps companies with talent acquisition, diversity & inclusion and employer branding. Audience: SME/ETI leaders and HR teams. The site had to make the offer clear fast, then get people to write.
Belgian constraint: the same prospect may search in NL, FR or EN. A classic one-pager has one URL: weak SEO, and you cannot share “Vision in Dutch”.
First screen: premium calm brand, one contact button. Simple hosting for an independent consultant: no server, no database, no subscription just for a form.
Framed around one goal: turn a visitor into a qualified contact. Non-technical presentation doc versioned with the code.

Single-page comfort with real addresses per section: /fr/home, /nl/about, /en/testimonials. Nine prerendered pages with title, description, canonical, hreflang and social previews. URL updates on scroll without reload; back button stays coherent.
Trade-off: no backend. Browser-validated form via EmailJS. Started with Resend (server route); switched to EmailJS for a fully static site with no server secret.

context.title: Product context
paragraphs: Targets: SME/ETI leaders, HR/TA, growing companies. Out of v1: blog, online booking, client area, analytics.
One repeated CTA: open the contact modal. Dutch default: any URL without a locale redirects there; choice is remembered.

architecture.title: Architecture
paragraphs: Front: Next.js 16 catch-all for 9 pages, OnePager assembles sections. IntersectionObserver updates the URL via history.replaceState. Middleware: 308 redirects, 1-year cookie, assets/sitemap/social images pass through.

Back: none. Copy in three translation files. Form RHF + Zod → EmailJS with typed success/error. Documented EmailJS pitfall: empty recipient → 422; config checked up front. Modal: focus trap, scroll lock, portal, success state.
Motion: GSAP for splash only, Framer Motion for modals, Web Animations API for fades.
bullets: hreflang fr-BE / nl-BE / en + x-default, ProfessionalService JSON-LD

decisions.title: Key decisions
paragraphs: URLs per section instead of # anchors (ignored by Google). April migration + sitemap hreflang. isProgrammaticScroll prevents URL flicker during menu-driven scrolling.
Accessibility as a feature: custom focus-trap hook, screen-reader form errors, splash skipped for prefers-reduced-motion.

Infinite loop bug, step by step. Splash animated then navigated to /home; timeline could restart → endless GET /home. Fix: cancellable timeline (cancel on unmount), navigate once. Shipped 5 minutes after the faulty refactor; same cancel pattern for reduced motion.
Robust site URL: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL then Vercel prod URL, force https, avoid Search Console duplicates.
bullets: Cancellable GSAP splash: no ghost animations
One Zod schema, small homemade adapter
No backend: zero server cost, zero server secret

execution.title: Delivery and next steps
paragraphs: 17/02/2026: architecture, i18n, menu, splash (loop bug fixed same night). 18/02: contact, Vision. 19/02: Testimonials, prod ready 0.1. V1 in three days. Then refactors, SEO, EmailJS, ennabv.be, per-locale routes (09/04). Last copy tweak 27/05.
Numbers: 44 commits on 8 active days, 3 PRs, 43 components, 9 pages, 3 languages.
Honesty: prioritized SEO, a11y and the form, shipped fast. Minimal tests (one render test), no CI. Next: route/SEO tests, GitHub Actions, light form anti-spam, client-validated testimonials.
